properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured on 0.77.0): the pointer check is a position in main()'s early-return dispatch, scoped to a client start, and every one-shot mode returns above it with an opener that creates a missing store. So --call AND --export in a pointer folder mint a fresh local design, exit 0, silent. The planned fix names only --call
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-10-02, triage agent A, on limitation 16 of art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02. Re-measures fact:a-cli-call-in-a-pointer-folder-mints-a-fresh-local-store-2026-10-01 (which recorded the ordering but said "NOT ROOT-CAUSED beyond the ordering") and walks the cause.

① OBSERVED (binary 0.77.0; origin/main is v0.77.0+3 commits, none in the dispatch). Scratch folder holding only `.reflow2.toml` ([design] id abc123def4567890, address http://127.0.0.1:9/g/abc123def4567890/mcp) and REFLOW2.md:
- `reflow2-mcp --call design_identity` → exit 0, stderr EMPTY, reply `{"graph_id":"041e1d6cc62cf8ed","label":"pf","origin":"minted"}`; `.reflow2/graph` plus id, meta, client and usage sidecars now exist.
- The next `--call loop_status` there → exit 0, `clean: true`, `next: []`. The stray design reads as a healthy empty one.
- `--graph-path .reflow2/graph --shared --only-if-present --call design_identity` (the user-scope entry's arguments) → the same: exit 0, a minted id, a store created.
- `--export` in a third pointer folder → exit 0, an empty design's export on stdout, and a store created. NEW: the defect is not --call's alone.
NOT AFFECTED: the stdio client in the same kind of folder (`--graph-path .reflow2/graph`, initialize + tools/list) printed "📍 THIS FOLDER NAMES ITS DESIGN … attached to that design", answered both requests with a connection error naming the pointer's address, and created nothing.
Logs: /home/ajs7/.claude/jobs/fa666a94/tmp/triage-A/measure.log (L16-a…d), l16/pf3-stdio.err.

② PRECEDENT: the 2026-10-01 fact (ordering only); fact:an-agent-opened-in-a-moved-designs-folder-is-served-the-frozen-store-2026-09-27 (the same class through the client door, which the pointer closed there).

③ CANDIDATES: (a) an ordering slip in main(); (b) a scope choice: the pointer's first slice was settled for "the client started in the folder" and nobody asked about one-shot modes; (c) the opener itself creates on open, so any path that skips a guard mints; (d) I measured the wrong thing (the folder layout is not one the pointer reads).

④/⑤ DISTINGUISHING MEASUREMENTS. (d) refuted: the stdio client in the identical folder found and followed the pointer. (b) confirmed from the record: the decision says "the client started in the folder attaches", cap:a-code-folder-names-its-design says "for any client start (not --http / --serve-shared servers)", and the code comment says "the pointer is the business of a CLIENT started in the folder". The only test (tests/a_code_folder_attaches_to_the_design_it_names.rs, three cases) starts a stdio client every time. (c) confirmed: --export, which shares no code with --call beyond opening, also mints. (a) is the trigger, not the cause: the guard is one position among early returns. --export ~1619, --call ~1631 and --import ~1640 return above it at ~1834, and so do --export-snapshot, --diff, --merge and --stop-shared; the latent --only-if-present check at ~1852 is below it too. That latent check is deliberately "after every CLI-only mode" by its own comment.

⑥ CLASS: whether a mode may open (and so create) the local store is decided by where its branch sits in main(), and the opener creates on open. A guard added for one entry point protects only the branches below it. The --call door's own design already knew the hazard in one case: it checks the tool name "BEFORE the graph is opened, so a typo never mints a graph directory" (cap:a-build-can-call-one-tool-from-the-shell-and-read-the-reply-as-json). But nothing checks the pointer or the store's existence first.

WHAT THIS ADDS TO THE PLAN. req:a-one-shot-call-never-creates-a-design-where-a-folder-names-one-on-a-server names `--call` only. A fix placed in call_one_tool would leave --export (and --import, which would write a whole design into a stray local store) open. A fix at the class would resolve the pointer (and --only-if-present) once, before ANY mode that opens a local store, and pin it with a test that runs every one-shot mode in a pointer folder and asserts no `.reflow2/` appears.

⑦ NOT DONE: no test written (no builds in this triage). ⑨ NOT MEASURED: --import, --diff and --merge in a pointer folder, which are inferred from the code ordering only, and a pointer folder that also holds a leftover store (by the code, --call opens that store and can write it).

ADDED THE SAME DAY (measured, log L16-e/f): the discovery calls the report's instructions file tells an agent to run FIRST also mint a store in a pointer folder. `--call find_tools --args '{"query":"where am i"}'` and `--call get_skill --args '{"name":"where-am-i"}'`, each in a fresh folder holding only `.reflow2.toml`, left a `.reflow2/` behind, although neither tool reads the design. call_one_tool builds its tool list from an in-memory probe, but then opens `--graph-path` for every tool alike. So a correct fix also covers tools that need no design at all. The "never run the door in such a folder" advice in the report cannot be followed, because the first command an agent runs there to find out what it is in already creates the stray design.
